title: Quantum-Geometric Design of Lattice Generalized Landau Levels
abstract: We design lattice models with tailored quantum geometry, including generalized Landau levels (LLs) satisfying the integrated trace condition and higher-Chern bands with ideal quantum geometry. Our models with $N=2$, $3$, and $4$ sublattices include a generalized Haldane model ($N=2$ honeycomb lattice model) with Gaussian-decaying hoppings realizable in twisted bilayer MoTe$_2$, and $N \geq 3$ models with exponentially decaying hoppings. Exact diagonalization reveals fractional Chern insulators in the generalized zeroth LL bands of all three models, a Moore-Read state in the generalized first LL band of the $N=4$ model, and various interaction-driven topological phases$\unicode{x2013}$including integer and fractional anomalous Hall crystals and a multicomponent Halperin state$\unicode{x2013}$in the ideal higher-Chern band of the $N=3$ model. Informed by quantum geometry, our work provides a pathway for lattice realizations of Landau-level and beyond-Landau-level physics.
summary: The paper details the quantum-geometric design of novel lattice models intended to host generalized Landau levels. By analyzing these structured systems using exact diagonalization and entanglement spectroscopy, the authors predict and confirm the realization of exotic correlated phases, including fractional Chern insulators and anomalous Hall crystal states.
main_problem: The research focuses on designing lattice models with tailored quantum geometry to realize physics analogous to Landau Levels (LLs) and higher-Chern bands, while also studying emergent fractionalized and charge-ordered states.
main_result: The authors successfully predict and confirm the existence of Abelian Fractional Chern Insulators (FCIs), Moore-Read states, and various anomalous Hall crystal phases in these engineered lattice models using exact diagonalization techniques.
method: The primary methods involve constructing generalized LLs via quantum geometry analysis and then employing Exact Diagonalization (ED) coupled with Particle Entanglement Spectrum (PES) analysis to study interacting electron physics on the resulting flat bands.
model_or_system: The models are lattice generalizations of Landau levels, constructed using $N=2, 3,$ and $4$ sublattices on lattices like honeycomb or kagome. The Hamiltonian is studied by projecting interactions onto selected bands derived from these engineered quantum geometries.
key_observables: Key observables include the Chern number ($C$), the quantum weight ($W$), the many-body average Chern number ($C_{	ext{avg}}$), and the analysis of entanglement gaps ($\xi_{AHC}$) to diagnose topological phases.
important_parameters:
Important parameters include filling fractions $
u$ (e.g., $1/3, 1/2, 1/5$), the number of sublattices ($N=2, 3, 4$), and hopping decay rates (Gaussian or exponential).
main_assumptions: Assumptions include the linear independence of basis states used in construction and that quantum geometry can be tailored to enforce specific topological properties.
figures_summary:
Figures illustrate band structures for different $N$ values, ED spectra showing quasi-degenerate ground states at fractional fillings (e.g., $
u=1/2$), and PES plots confirming gaps associated with charge ordering.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from designing the lattice models based on quantum geometry to analyzing the resulting flat bands via ED for various filling fractions, culminating in the identification of specific correlated topological phases like FCIs and AHCs.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it provides a concrete theoretical framework—using engineered lattice Hamiltonians—to model exotic many-body phenomena (like fractional quantum Hall states) that are central to condensed matter theory, bridging geometric design with strong correlation physics.
